turns.text: I retry the payment after a timeout, and that is where the shit starts. I reserve stock, call the payment service, and on `UpstreamTimeoutError` I run the same charge again with no idempotency key, which is a lovely way to double-bill people [orders/checkout.ts:38-57].

I record every successful charge, but I never check whether `order_id` was already charged before calling the card network, so the same order can slide through twice. The ledger is kept in memory and `recordCharge` just pushes a new entry, damn near begging for duplicates when the caller retries [payments/processor.ts:29-49; payments/ledger.ts:11-19].

I cut upstream calls off at `2000ms`, and the payment path usually takes about `2400ms`, so I hand orders a timeout and let them panic-retry. That is a clean little timeout gamble, and it lands like shit when the caller has no safe repeat token [gateway/config.ts:15-16; gateway/proxy.ts:25-49; payments/processor.ts:23-28].

I do stop on `paid`, but only after the charge comes back, so that does not save this mess. The retry loop still fires on a timeout, and the code even says it was added to fix flaky checkouts, which is the kind of damn sentence that ages badly [orders/checkout.ts:43-57; orders/checkout.ts:67-69].

I can prove the duplicate pattern: `sample-charges.log` shows the same `orderId=ord_8f3k2b61` charged twice with two different `chargeId`s. My processor waits for the card network, then writes a fresh ledger entry every time, so a repeated request is not safe to repeat [payments/logs/sample-charges.log:6-7; payments/processor.ts:33-49].

I am not innocent, but I am not the one minting duplicate charges. I timeout first, then `orders` retries, and `payments` has no dedupe check before `recordCharge`, so this damn chain only needs one timeout to turn into two charges [gateway/proxy.ts:29-53; orders/checkout.ts:44-57; payments/processor.ts:33-49].

verdict.rootCause: The gateway times out the payment call at 2000ms, but the payment path usually takes about 2400ms. `orders` retries after that timeout, and `payments` does not check whether the same `order_id` was already charged, so the repeated request creates a second charge instead of reusing the first one.
verdict.judgeLine: gateway set the trap at 2000ms, and `orders` walked straight into it.
